---
title: "Step 1 — Install R and RStudio"
subtitle: "Step 1 of 5"
---

**Time:** 25 minutes, plus download time.
**Before you start:** the laptop you will bring to IISc, and administrator
rights on it.
**When you finish:** R and RStudio are installed and working together.

You are installing 2 programs. **R** does the work. **RStudio** is the window
you look at it through. Install R first.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Check your administrator rights now
You may not have them on an institutional laptop. Find out this week, not on
Sunday night. If you cannot install software yourself, send this page to your
IT department today.
:::

## Step 1 of 5 — Install R

1. Go to [cran.r-project.org](https://cran.r-project.org).
2. Click the link for your operating system.
3. **Windows:** click **base**, then the download link. Run the `.exe`. Accept
   every default.
4. **macOS:** click the `.pkg` for your chip. Apple Silicon (M1, M2, M3, M4)
   needs the **arm64** build. Older Intel Macs need the plain one.
5. **Linux:** follow the CRAN instructions for your distribution.

**You should see:** an installer that finishes with no error box.

**If it does not work:** install into the default location. A folder path with
spaces or non-English characters in it breaks package installs later.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Not sure which Mac you have?
Click the Apple menu, then **About This Mac**. Read the **Chip** line.
:::

## Step 2 of 5 — Check that R opens

1. Open R on its own. On Windows, choose **R x64** from the Start menu. On
   macOS, open `R.app`.
2. Read the first line in the console window.

**You should see:** a version number of **4.1.0 or higher**.

**If it does not work:** repeat Step 1. Do not go on until R itself opens.

## Step 3 of 5 — Install RStudio

1. Go to
   [posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop](https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/).
2. Download the installer the page offers you.
3. Run it. Accept the defaults.

**You should see:** RStudio open with 4 panes. The console at the left shows
the same R version you read in Step 2.

**If it does not work:** if the console says R is missing, close RStudio. Check
that R itself opens. Then install RStudio again.

::: {.callout-note}
## R and RStudio are 2 different programs
Updating one does not update the other. When you update, you have 2 things to
update.
:::

## Step 4 of 5 — Point RStudio at the right R

Skip this step if you have never used R on this laptop.

More than one R can be installed at once. Check which one RStudio picked.

1. In RStudio, click **Tools → Global Options → General**.
2. Read the **R version** line at the top.

**You should see:** the R you installed in Step 1.

**If it does not work:** click **Change**, choose the right R, then restart
RStudio.

## Step 5 of 5 — Test the pipe

1. Click once inside the **Console** pane, at the bottom left.
2. Type `c(1, 2, 3) |> sum()` and press **Enter**.

**You should see:** `[1] 6`.

**If it does not work:** an error here means your R is older than 4.1.0. Go
back to Step 1.

::: {.callout-note}
## Why this matters
RStudio looks for R when it starts. Install them the other way round and
RStudio reports that R is missing, even when it is not.

`|>` is the pipe. We use it in every session, so Step 5 is a real test.
:::

## Done?
